written.myAnswer: An entrepreneur is a person who starts or organizes a business, often taking risks to pursue an opportunity. The word comes from the French entreprendre, meaning “to undertake.”
Digital technologies help entrepreneurs advertise and sell online, communicate with customers, and take orders from people in different places, extending their reach beyond the local area.

An e-commerce platform is an online system through which a business displays and sells goods or services. It enables customers to browse and place orders online, helping the business reach a wider market.
Identifying market needs helps an entrepreneur develop a product or service that addresses a real customer demand, making the business idea more likely to attract buyers.
Design thinking aims to develop effective, creative solutions by understanding users’ needs, generating ideas, and testing and improving possible solutions.

Market analysis helps a business understand its customers, their needs, and its competitors so it can make informed decisions about products and strategies. For example, a Lahore bakery could research local tastes and prices at nearby bakeries before deciding what to offer and how much to charge.

A revenue model explains how a business earns income, such as by selling products or charging for services. It is essential because it shows how the business plans to bring in money and support its costs.

Businesses can contribute by using resources efficiently, reducing waste and pollution, and adopting cleaner energy. These actions support SDG7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).

Entrepreneurship contributes to economic growth by creating businesses, jobs, and income. Entrepreneurs also introduce new products and services and respond to customer needs. For example, a business using mobile apps or an e-commerce platform can sell beyond its local area. Such activity can encourage competition and improve services.

Market research tools, such as surveys, help a business learn about customer needs and competitors. Online marketing tools can promote products suited to those needs, while an e-commerce platform displays products and takes orders. Together, they help a business make informed decisions, reach customers, and generate sales.

The design thinking process involves empathizing with users, defining their problem, generating ideas, creating a prototype, and testing it. For farmers in rural Pakistan, a team could learn about their difficulties getting weather or crop information, define the key problem, develop ideas for a simple mobile service, build a prototype, and test it with farmers. Their feedback could guide improvements before launch.

The bookstore would research students’ reading habits, preferred subjects, budgets, and buying methods, then compare local bookshops and online sellers. It could earn money by selling new and second-hand textbooks, exam guides, and other books, and possibly by charging delivery fees. It could promote its stock through social media, student groups, a website, and online offers. An online ordering system could display available books and receive orders, with local delivery serving students in the area.

Use detailed explanations and practical Pakistan-based examples, such as researching students’ book needs, comparing nearby shops, selling textbooks and exam guides online, promoting through student social media groups, and arranging local delivery.

A solar-panel installation business in Pakistan can support SDG7 by helping homes and businesses access clean energy. Socially, it can improve access to electricity and create jobs. Environmentally, solar power can reduce reliance on fossil fuels and related pollution. Economically, the business generates income and employment, while customers may save on electricity costs over time.
